messages:
maria (support): customer reported repeated EventSource disconnects in Safari when connecting through our CDN. They see partial events, then a silent disconnect. Repro steps pasted below from customer. filing here so eng can triage.

maria (support): REPRO (as reported):
1) open Safari (macOS, 16.4)
2) open console, run page with: \n```html
<script>
  const es = new EventSource("https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?session=abc123");
  es.onmessage = e => console.log('MSG', e.data);
  es.onerror = e => console.log('ES ERROR', e);
</script>
```
3) after ~20s: client logs stop, no `onclose` visible, page still shows connected, no further events. Refresh reconnects and emits remaining backlog but user complains partial outputs seen in product (missing tokens).

maria (support): customer provided edge response headers (from devtools network -> response headers):
```
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
cache-control: public, max-age=31536000
x-amz-cf-id: xxxxx
via: 2.0 cloudfront
connection: keep-alive
```

jess (frontend): @kai this looks like a CDN/edge caching problem — SSE should never be cached. also need to check CORS + credentials. can you confirm what headers our stream path returns from origin?

kai (eng-runtime): copied notes: streaming endpoints must opt out of edge caching and transformation. immediate suspects: CloudFront is caching the stream (max-age huge) and might be serving a cached 200 or injecting buffering that breaks Safari's EventSource. Safari is picky about chunked flushes and HTTP/2 multiplexing + edge idle timeouts. we need: `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate`, `Surrogate-Control: no-store`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (origin-level), and avoid `Content-Encoding: gzip` on the stream. also remove `Content-Length`.

kai (eng-runtime): additional CORS / creds note: if customers use EventSource with credentials, Access-Control-Allow-Origin must be an explicit origin (wildcard `*` won't work with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`). Safari historically rejects connections if these mismatch.

maria (support): customer also shared the fetch command they used to inspect headers: `curl -i -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?session=abc123`
returned headers (again):
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
cache-control: public, max-age=31536000
content-encoding: br
```

jess (frontend): `content-encoding: br` on SSE is bad — edge might compress and then buffer until a block is full, Safari expects incremental chunks. compression + long max-age = recipe for silent stalls.

kai (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation steps:
- add edge behavior to disable caching for `/v1/stream*` (forward all headers, query strings, and set `Cache-Control: no-store` at edge).
- disable compression at CDN for that path (CloudFront compresses by default for some content types).
- ensure origin sends `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` and no `content-encoding` header.
- add Keep-Alive/idle ping (send a comment line `: ping\n\n` every 15s) so some middleboxes don't close due to apparent idle.

jess (frontend): client fallback idea: for Safari specifically, we can fallback to fetch+ReadableStream (experimental) which gives us more control over reconnects and partial data handling. snippet: 
```
if (window.EventSource && !isSafari) {
  new EventSource(url)
} else {
  // fetch + stream parser fallback
}
```
note: event-source-polyfill is helpful but some older Safari versions still mis-handle reconnect timing.

maria (support): policy/ops ask: is there any risk to turning off caching for `/v1/stream` systematically? will it affect cost?

kai (eng-runtime): it's fine; streams are low qps relative to embeddings/generation requests. disabling edge cache for that path is expected and safest. cost impact minimal. we should also ensure cache key doesn't drop query string tokens — if CloudFront caches by path only, the token query could be stripped and different clients see mixed streams (yikes). confirm cache key includes query string if any sensitive tokens used in query. better: require Authorization header instead of token-in-query.

jess (frontend): +1 on requiring Authorization header. also for Safari quirk: if you see `EventSource.readyState === 0` but no `onerror` fires, adding a small client-side timer to detect no events for N seconds and then force `es.close(); new EventSource(url)` has helped customers.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled by @kai: `edge-config` change to disable caching & compression for `/v1/stream*` — https://deploys.redwood-internal/ops/12345 (ETA ~25m) :gear:

maria (support): thanks @kai @jess. i'll tell the customer to test again in ~30m after the edge change. i'll report back with their logs. also asked them to switch to Authorization header and retry if possible.

kai (eng-runtime): followups (post-deploy): please capture a `curl -i -N` after deploy and paste headers here. we'll also add periodic ping on origin side to reduce edge idle kills.

maria (support): noted. customer will try after deploy and let us know. :thumbsup:
